# Clean Voice Audio

- Route: `/tools/clean-voice-audio`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `clean-voice-audio`

## Summary

Make speech clearer by reducing hiss, room tone and rumble in podcasts, interviews and voice memos. (AI tools)

## Details

A phone voice memo in an echoey kitchen, a podcast guest on a laptop microphone, a lecture recorded from the back of the room: the words are there, but they sit under hiss and room sound. Clean Voice runs the recording through DeepFilterNet on our GPU, then through a fixed broadcast-style polish chain that trims rumble, caps the top end, brings the level to a consistent loudness and stops peaks from clipping. It is built for talking, not for music.
### What it does
- Converts your upload to 48 kHz mono with ffmpeg, which is the input DeepFilterNet expects, and hands that WAV to the model on our GPU.
- Suppresses steady background sound (hiss, fans, hum, room tone) while keeping the speech, using the DeepFilterNet enhancement network.
- Applies a polish chain after denoising: an 80 Hz high-pass, a 14 kHz low-pass, loudness normalisation to -16 LUFS with a -1.5 dBTP true-peak ceiling, and a limiter at 0.95.
- Encodes the result in the format you choose: MP3, AAC or OGG at 192 kbps, Opus at 128 kbps, FLAC, or 16-bit WAV.
- Skips the standard bitrate, EQ, effect and trim controls, since the AI path replaces the normal ffmpeg filter pipeline.
### How to use it
1. Upload a recording: Voice memos, interview audio, podcast takes or lecture captures in MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, AAC, OGG or Opus.
2. Clean Voice is preset: The operation is fixed on this page; the only choice left is the output format.
3. Normalise, denoise, polish: ffmpeg makes a 48 kHz mono WAV, DeepFilterNet denoises it, and the polish filters set the tone and loudness.
4. Download and listen: Compare with the original on headphones before you publish it.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, flac, m4a, aac, ogg, opus
- Output: mp3, wav, flac, m4a, ogg
- Clean Voice uses the everyday allowance; length limits depend on your plan and are shown live in the form.
### Technical details
- The polish chain is exactly highpass=f=80,lowpass=f=14000,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11,alimiter=limit=0.95, applied once to the denoised WAV. The high-pass removes handling rumble and plosive thumps, the low-pass tames hiss above 14 kHz, and loudnorm brings the integrated loudness to -16 LUFS, the usual target for spoken-word podcasts.
- Output is always mono at 48 kHz because the model runs on a single channel. A stereo interview stays intelligible but loses its left-right placement; if you need stereo, this is the wrong tool.
- Encoder settings come from the output extension: libmp3lame at 192 kbps for MP3, aac at 192 kbps for AAC or M4A, libvorbis at 192 kbps for OGG, libopus at 128 kbps for Opus, flac for FLAC and pcm_s16le for WAV. There is no bitrate selector on the AI path.
- Trim ranges and the usual effects are ignored when an AI operation is selected; the converter routes the file straight to the model and returns. Trim the recording first if you only want part of it cleaned.
- A second pass through Clean Voice re-normalises audio that is already at -16 LUFS and can add a watery quality to consonants. Run it once.
- The model struggles with competing voices, music beds and sudden loud events; those are not "steady background" and are largely left in place.
### When not to use it
Skip this tool for music, singing or anything where the background is part of the sound you want to keep: the model treats everything that is not speech as noise, and the polish chain cuts below 80 Hz and above 14 kHz, which hollows out instruments. It is also the wrong choice when you need to keep stereo, when the recording is clipped or distorted (that damage is not noise and cannot be filtered out), or when you only want the noise lowered without any change to level or tone, which is what the Remove Background Noise page does instead.
### Use cases
- Podcasts and interviews: Tidy a remote guest recorded on a basic microphone and bring them to the same loudness as the host.
- Voice memos and dictation: Make a phone recording understandable later, and loud enough to hear without headphones.
- Lectures and meetings: Lower the air-conditioning hum and projector fan in a recording taken from the back of a room.
- Narration for a video: Polish voice-over before placing it in the Darkroom editor.
### FAQ
Q: Why does the cleaned file come out mono?
A: The pipeline converts every input to one channel at 48 kHz before DeepFilterNet runs, and encodes the model output as it is. A stereo recording therefore returns as mono. For a two-microphone interview, split the channels first and clean each one separately if you need to keep the separation.
Q: What loudness does Clean Voice normalise to?
A: The polish chain uses ffmpeg loudnorm with an integrated target of -16 LUFS, a true-peak ceiling of -1.5 dBTP and a loudness range of 11 LU, followed by a limiter at 0.95. That matches common spoken-word delivery targets, so an episode cleaned here will sit at a similar level to professionally mastered podcasts.
Q: Can I set the bitrate or trim the file on this page?
A: No. When an AI operation is active the converter routes straight to the model and ignores the bitrate, EQ, effects and trim settings. The output rate is fixed by the format: 192 kbps for MP3, AAC and OGG, 128 kbps for Opus. Trim the recording on another tool first if you only want part of it.
Q: How is this different from Remove Background Noise?
A: Both run the same DeepFilterNet model. Clean Voice adds the high-pass, low-pass, loudness normalisation and limiter afterwards; Remove Background Noise stops at the denoised signal and leaves your levels and tone alone. Pick Clean Voice for a finished spoken-word file and the other page when you plan to mix or master it yourself.
Q: Can it fix a recording that is clipped or distorted?
A: No. Clipping is missing waveform, not added noise, and the model has nothing to subtract. It can still lower the hiss around a distorted take, but the crunch on loud syllables will remain.
Q: How many recordings can I clean per day, and is it free?
A: Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. The current table is on /pricing.
